diagrams.title: From editing intent to graph observation
diagrams.summary: The graph changes through commands, is committed and validated, then is evaluated by a distinct runtime.

nodes.label: Graph commit
nodes.description: The authority commits a new revision.

nodes.label: Validation
nodes.description: Connections, types and dialect rules are checked.

diagrams.caption: A Composition-backed Nodal projection is neither the canonical Composition nor its runtime.

diagrams.title: Scope a projection presentation
diagrams.summary: A host owns presentation contributions and exposes them only while its registry is active.

nodes.label: Created
nodes.description: The host creates an empty scoped registry.

nodes.label: Registered
nodes.description: Versioned contributions target a dialect and projection kind.

nodes.label: Inactive
nodes.description: Resolution falls back without deleting declarations.

nodes.label: Disposed
nodes.description: Contributions are released and the registry cannot be reused.

diagrams.caption: Importing a domain specialization does not mutate presentation state owned by another host.

diagrams.title: Resolve a dialect without merging responsibilities
diagrams.summary: A host registers schema, admission and execution independently, then resolves one runtime view for a selected dialect.

nodes.label: Schema contributions
nodes.description: Declare node types, ports and defaults.

nodes.label: Admission contributions
nodes.description: Validate domain rules without executing nodes.

nodes.label: Execution contributions
nodes.description: Bind admitted node types to runtime functions.

nodes.label: Host registry
nodes.description: Reject duplicate targets and expose contributions only while active.

nodes.label: Resolved dialect runtime
nodes.description: Keep schema, admission and execution as distinct lanes.

nodes.label: Compatibility bundle
nodes.description: Temporarily serve callers that still accept one dialect value.

diagrams.caption: The compatibility bundle is derived from the resolved contributions and does not own their lifecycle.
